declared.title: Choice overload reduces neural signatures of choice set value in dorsal striatum and anterior cingulate cortex
declared.foundIn: rapport contre-preuve reports/too-many-choices/counter-evidence.md (2026-11-22), DOI trouvé par ses requêtes ; titre relevé sur Crossref par la session : contrôle d'identité plus faible ; déjà repérée par la recherche Crossref « choice overload reduces neural signatures of choice set value » du dossier

population: participants in an fMRI scanner choosing from, or browsing, sets of 6, 12 or 24 items; sample size and country not given in the abstract

findings.text: Brain value signals were highest for 12-item sets, judged « the right amount »; 6 items felt too few and 24 too many

support.sentence: Activity was highest for 12-item sets, which were perceived as having 'the right amount' of options and was lower for 6-item and 24-item sets, which were perceived as 'too small' and 'too large', respectively.

limits: brain activity and judged set size, not satisfaction with the item chosen
small brain-imaging sample (size not in the abstract)
same first author as reutskaja-2009-satiate and reutskaja-2022-deprivation
